subject: The count was prose - and a finding I had to retract within the hour
body:
Fifth version. This one is mostly about the campaign's own honesty, and it contains a
retraction of something I nearly told you as a finding.

THE COUNT WAS PROSE. I built a script that runs every criterion checker and reads the verdicts out
of the artefacts instead of out of my own notes. First time the number has been computed rather
than remembered across ninety-three hand-offs. What it found:

    16 of the 40 criteria have an automated checker at all.
    Of those: 7 MET, 4 NOT MET, 5 ambiguous.
    The other 21 rest entirely on prose.

The standing "37 of 45" is therefore not reproducible from the instruments. I don't think it is
wrong -- most of those 21 were judged on real evidence when they were judged. But it is not
auditable, and I am not going to keep quoting it as if it were. The honest version is: 7 criteria
are MET by something that runs today, 21 are MET by something I wrote down.

A CRITERION HAD SILENTLY STOPPED BEING TRUE. C3.3 says every IC must be published as a curve
across horizons, never as a single point -- because a point cannot tell "no signal" from "not at
the horizon you happened to measure". It was recorded MET on Sunday. It was not met this morning,
and nobody broke it: new scripts written since had quietly reintroduced the defect. Five of them.
All the same way. The fifth was written by me an hour after I fixed the other four, while I was
literally typing a comment about how this kept happening.

So I stopped trying to remember the convention and made the defect unwritable. Result files now go
through a writer that runs the C3.3 check BEFORE the file exists and throws an error naming the bad
node instead of writing it. Wired into all 36 scripts. That is the actual fix; the five repairs
were symptoms.

NOW THE RETRACTION, and it is the part I want you to read.

While fixing that, I measured the components directly from the export instead of scraping the EA's
log, and comp_mtf came back NEGATIVE against forward returns at every horizon from 5 minutes to
nearly a day, growing steadily to -0.19. The EA's own readings for the same component are POSITIVE.
comp_mtf is the input your traded direction agrees with 83.5% of the time.

I concluded the system was pointed backwards by its dominant input. I spent an hour on it. It is
wrong, and here is why:

    comp_mtf vs forward return, h=21                  -0.0640
    comp_mtf vs DIRECTION x forward return, h=21      +0.0438

They are two different questions. The EA scores components against the R-multiple of a trade whose
direction it sets from the same signals comp_mtf is built from -- so its measurement is
direction-conditioned. Mine wasn't. A trade earns direction x return, not return. The sign flips on
conditioning and it has to.

And the uncomfortable part: the EA's target is the BETTER one. It has been measuring the
economically correct quantity since a fix labelled FIX52. Every IC curve in my research layer,
including the ones I have been sending you all night, has been measuring a quantity nobody trades.

What survives is small: on the target that matters, comp_mtf is +0.0438 at a 21-bar hold, z=2.13
against a bar of 4.03. Right direction. Not close to significant. The component is not backwards.
It is also not informative.

ONE THING TO FIX IN THE EA, and it is not the direction logic. The calibration prints these as
"MTF=+0.12" next to five other component names with no statement of what they were measured
against. That is exactly what let me misread a bracket-conditioned R-multiple as a forward-return
IC while holding both numbers. One label on one line. I have not applied it -- run 5 is live and the
deploy rule is absolute -- so it is queued for the next window.

Run 5 reached the purge/embargo stage tonight and is still going. It is the third calibration
C6.3/C6.4 need.
